text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA - Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski has produced 30 amendment proposals to the version of a new constitution passed by both houses of parliament last Friday.

Kwasniewski proposed that verdicts of the Constitutional Tribunal should be final, taxes should not threaten the minimum standard of living of people who earn their income through work, and parliamentary immunity rights should only cover issues concerning a parliamentarian's professional obligations.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The average Pole spends 40 percent of income on food products, the state trade supervision body (PIH) said.
However, quality standards in several groups of food articles, such as pasta, confectionery, non-alcoholic beverages and tinned meat and vegetables have been declining each year.
- The treasury ministry has proposed that National Investment Fund (NFI) certificates should expire at the end of 1998.
NFI certificate holders will have to convert them to NFI shares by that time, the ministry said.
- The Huta Katowice steel mill needs investment of $1 billion to start production of sheet products.
Last year's production of long semi-products brought the mill losses of several tens of million zlotys, the plant's spokeswoman Renata Bytomska said.
Following the withdrawal of Belgium's Sidmar, Huta Katowice has been negotiating with other investors, though it is too early to give any details, Bytomska said.
- In mid-1997 the listed industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim will start restructuring its operations, the company's president Andrzej Skowronski said.
By the end of April the company will receive money from the sale of convertible bonds, Skowronski said.

- The extraordianry shareholders' meeting of the Daewoo Motor Polska commercial vehicle maker in Lublin, eastern Poland, has increased the company's share capital from 30.8 million zlotys to 231.4 million zlotys through a share issue of 308,500 shares to be taken over by Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd. and Daewoo Corporation.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Ruch press distribution chain will be privatised by the end of June 1997, Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz said.

- Credit granted by the Bank Pekao SA to the bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard will allow the yard to complete the building of a vessel now under construction and give employment to 800 workers, Cimoszewicz said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Dutch Sphinx Gustavsberg will buy the WZS sanitary porcelain plant in Wroclaw, southwestern Poland, worth 8.8 million guilders, the company said.
PARKIET
- The Eurofundusz 2 aggressive investment fund, controlled by the TFP Przymierze trust fund company, will start to sell investment units on April 14.
By year-end the association will launch two other funds, TFP Przymierze's deputy president Wojciech Gryko said.
